Additional props passed to Downshift. **Use with caution:** anything you define here overrides the components' internal handling of that prop. Downshift APIs and internals are subject to change, and in some cases they can not be shimmed by Carbon to shield you from potentially breaking changes.
Allow users to pass in arbitrary items from their collection that are pre-selected
Specify if the currently selected value is invalid.
Provide the text that is displayed when the control is in an invalid state
Specify if the `FluidMultiSelect` should render its menu items in condensed mode
Specify if the `FluidMultiSelect` should render the `filterable` variant of `FluidMultiSelect`
Renders an item as a custom React node instead of a string.

Helper function passed to downshift that allows the library to render a given item to a string label. By default, it extracts the `label` field from a given item to serve as the item label in the list. Consider declaring function with `useCallback` to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
We try to stay as generic as possible here to allow individuals to pass in a collection of whatever kind of data structure they prefer
Generic `label` that will be used as the textual representation of what this field is for
Specify the locale of the control. Used for the default `compareItems` used for sorting the list of items in the control.
`onChange` is a utility for this controlled component to communicate to a consuming component what kind of internal state changes are occurring.
**Filterable variant only** - `onInputValueChange` is a utility for this controlled component to communicate to the currently typed input.
`onMenuChange` is a utility for this controlled component to communicate to a consuming component that the menu was open(`true`)/closed(`false`).
Whether or not the Multiselect is readonly
For full control of the selected items
Specify feedback (mode) of the selection. `top`: selected item jumps to top `fixed`: selected item stays at it's position `top-after-reopen`: selected item jump to top after reopen dropdown

Provide a method that sorts all options in the control. Overriding this prop means that you also have to handle the sort logic for selected versus un-selected items. If you just want to control ordering, consider the `compareItems` prop instead.
